methodStanding: In short: we follow each euro of spending through the firms that are paid, and their suppliers, using OECD tables of who buys what from whom. We count the wages and profits it supports in each country. The figures are estimates of what the spending supports, not a count of new activity.

what.headline: Wages and profits supported at home (economists call this value added), divided by all modelled spend, from the first year through the year on the screen. The low and high figures push every assumption the same way at once, so they are a stress test, not a likely range.
what.output: Money paid to firms in this place, out of every euro spent so far.
what.outputAbroad: Money paid to firms abroad, out of every euro spent so far.
what.kept: Wages and profits kept by firms in this place.
what.keptAbroad: Wages and profits kept by firms abroad.
what.passed: Purchases those firms pass on to their suppliers.
what.productTax: Product taxes. For firms in one place this is their output, minus what they keep, minus what they pass on.
what.added: Wages and profits at home, wages and profits abroad and product taxes, added up. The part kept at home is the headline.
what.country: Wages and profits supported in {place}, summed across the tiers, for spend up to the year on the slider.
what.industry: Wages and profits supported at home in {place}.
what.constructionJobs: Jobs supported by capital spend during the build, counted where the work is done. A job is a person employed, as the source counts it, so a part-time job counts as one job.
what.ongoingJobs: The yearly average of jobs supported after the build, including staff, suppliers and refresh spend. A job is a person employed, as the source counts it, so a part-time job counts as one job.
what.carbonNet: Embodied greenhouse gases plus operational electricity, minus the heat offset. CO2e counts all greenhouse gases as the amount of carbon dioxide that would warm the climate as much.
what.embodied: Greenhouse gases embodied in purchases, counted as CO2e. Electricity is left out here so it is not counted twice.
what.operational: Megawatt-hours of electricity times the factor for the view you chose. When heat recovery is on, the heat pumps' electricity is included.
what.offset: Greenhouse gases displaced by heat delivered to a network, counted as CO2e. It counts only when heat recovery is on.
what.energy: Electricity the site uses in a year of operation. The IT equipment uses its capacity times its average use, over every hour of the year. Power usage effectiveness (PUE) scales that up to the whole site. Every year of operation uses the same amount.
what.energyIt: Electricity for the servers, storage and network: the capacity times its average use, over every hour of the year.
what.energyOther: Electricity for cooling, lighting and power losses: the IT electricity times the PUE, minus the IT electricity.
what.energyHeat: Electricity for the heat pumps that raise the servers' heat to the temperature the local network needs. It counts only when heat recovery is on.
what.compare: Wages and profits at home per euro spent on construction in this country, from the same tables. It is a yardstick for any building project, such as housing or a warehouse.
what.gridVa: Wages and profits at home in an average year of operation, divided by the grid connection the site needs: the IT load times the power usage effectiveness (PUE).
what.gridJobs: Jobs supported in an average year of operation, divided by the grid connection the site needs.
what.payroll: Wages paid to the operator's own staff in a year of operation. This is wages and profits at home, in IT services.
what.crossBorder: The share of those wages paid to people who live across the border. It does not reduce wages and profits at home.
what.spend: Spend on {name} up to the year on the slider.
what.va: Wages and profits supported in {place} at {tier}.
what.tax: Net product taxes at {tier}. This is part of the flow. It is not shown as its own result.
what.onward: Purchases that move on to suppliers after {tier}.
what.other: Smaller country groups at {tier}, grouped so the flow stays readable.
what.size: IT load. Schedules are per MW, so one MW matches the file until you set a size.
what.slider: The share of {name} bought from home rather than imported. The starting point is the national average.
what.heat: Heat recovery spend, the heat pumps' electricity, and the heat offset. They count only when this is on. It starts off because two inputs are estimates: the share of the servers' heat a local network can take, and the carbon of the heat it would replace.
what.year: The year on the slider. Marks show the build, the first IT fit-out, each refresh and the mid-life refresh.
what.staff: Payroll is the operator's own wages and profits, at home, in IT services, with no carbon. Operator staff are persons employed, counted the same way as other jobs, not from an industry rate.
